sections.html: Hurricane lies in southwestern Utah at the eastern end of the St. George area, and the Virgin River hugs nearly the whole northern boundary. Between 2010 and 2020 the population rose 45.7% to 20,036, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 25,745. Of 8,035 housing units counted in 2020, 13.1% stood vacant, so an empty house is a common sight and buyers have plenty of choices.

Hurricane began in 1896 as part of the Cotton Mission, and small farms around town still grow peaches, pecans and pistachios. Sand Hollow State Park has a 1,322-acre reservoir with camping and trails, and Quail Creek State Park offers a 600-acre reservoir and a campground. Distribution centers and an annual mountain bike festival bring work and visitors. A recreational trail follows the old Hurricane Canal, dry since 1985. Mentioning the lakes and trails helps a listing, but out-of-area shoppers still judge the house on heat, water and upkeep.

Summers are brutal. The nearest long-term weather record, from St. George, puts the typical July high near 101.9 degrees, with about 60 afternoons each year at 100 or hotter. Rainfall is only about 9 inches. Nights drop to 32 degrees or lower on roughly 60 mornings a year, and monsoon storms arrive from mid-July to mid-September.

Shoppers will ask about the age of the roof and the cooling system, so find those dates before the first showing. Look over the drainage around the lot too, since monsoon downpours show weak spots fast.

Water has made headlines here before. The Quail Creek dike, part of an offstream reservoir run by the Washington County Water Conservancy District, gave way at 12:30 a.m. on January 1, 1989 and released about 25,000 acre-feet. Damage ran to about $12 million, with no deaths.

You can reach city offices at 147 N 870 W or by calling 435-635-2811. Business licensing is handled inside Planning and Zoning, and a home-based business can be approved under Title 10, Chapter 42 of city code.

Students attend Washington County schools, and Hurricane High School runs grades 10 to 12. Hurricane operates its own electric utility, which reports delivering power 99.9846% of the time. Fire response comes from the Hurricane Valley Fire District.

Section 3-10-11 of city code requires a business license for any short-term rental. Single-family zones have a cap, and no second rental license may sit within 300 feet of an existing one.

Rental ruleHurricane requirement
License cap, single-family zonesThree licenses per 1,000 residents
SpacingNo other rental with a license within 300 feet
ParkingOne off-street space per bedroom
OccupancyTen, unless the fire district approves more with suppression
Complaint responseWithin one hour
FinesUp to $750 per violation, and each day counts

The license stays behind when you sell. Within 45 days of closing, the new owner must apply for a fresh one or the old one is forfeited, and then the buyer would need to reapply or wait in line. Say so at the start if the house has been a rental, because an investor may value that license as part of the price.

Washington County real property tax comes due every November 30, whether or not a notice reached you. Neighbors received one and you did not? Call the Treasurer for a copy. There are no payment plans, but any partial payment of $10 or more per parcel is accepted at any time.

  • Each payment covers interest first, then penalty, then tax. When several years are delinquent, Utah law sends the money to the newest year first.
  • The Clerk-Auditor holds a sale each May for properties delinquent five years or more.
  • Utah bans the sale of tax liens and tax lien certificates.

The tax is a lien on the land and not a debt of the person, and the title company divides the bill between buyer and seller on a mid-year sale. The Treasurer works from 111 East Tabernacle St. in St. George and answers at 435-301-7720.

Valuation appeals run on a state deadline: the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor sends notice. A main home is taxed on 55% of market value. Buyers must file their own claim for that exemption after they purchase.

Closing takes place at a title company, and the deed then goes to the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle in St. George. Recordings are not taken after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, so a late signing may be filed the next day. The Recorder's phone is 435-301-7680.

A deed must name the grantees, give a mailing address for tax billing and include a proper legal description. The signature must match the name of the owner of record, which is worth confirming at the start for an inherited house.

When a bill is still open at closing, it is paid from your proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff amount and hand it to the title officer. Since the lien follows the land, clearing it is built into every closing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Hurricane
sections.html:
Start by giving us the address and basic details. We tour the house, check what sold nearby, and make an offer you are free to decline. After you accept, a title company searches the record, chooses a closing date and files the deed. With no lender in the picture, you avoid an appraisal wait and a bank's repair demands.

A relative in another state can still sign, since the title company can set up remote signatures. For an empty house, the monthly drain of tax, utilities and insurance stops when the sale closes.

Before you call, pull the deed, the most recent tax notice, utility account details and any rental license paperwork. If the roof or cooling system is old, note roughly when it was installed. Buyers and title officers both ask for these items, and having them ready shortens the whole process.

Three routes exist: hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. A listing demands showings while newer houses compete down the road. A cash buyer takes the property in present condition.

  • Empty houses still racking up tax, utility and insurance costs.
  • Short-term rentals that lost a license or fell short of city rules.
  • Inherited houses with heirs living out of state.
  • Older homes with tired roofs, evaporative coolers or failing air conditioning.

From any buyer, request a written closing date and proof of funds. Then set the number beside what a listing would bring home once repairs and commission come out.

faqs.a: The 2020 count was 20,036 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 25,745.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in Hurricane?
faqs.a: Every November 30, billed by the Washington County Treasurer, even if no notice arrives. There are no payment plans, but partial payments of $10 or more are accepted.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental license transfer when I sell my Hurricane house?
faqs.a: No. The new owner has 45 days from purchase to apply for a fresh license, or the old one is forfeited. The buyer could then land on a waiting list.

faqs.q: Is Hurricane's climate hard on houses?
faqs.a: Yes, it can be. St. George, the nearest long-term station, averages a July high near 102 degrees with about 60 days a year at 100 or more, which wears on roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Hurricane house?
faqs.a: With the Washington County Recorder in St. George. Recordings are cut off at 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and the title company usually files the deed for you.
